title: Gaussian Algebraic Inclusion versus Nested Markov Inclusion for Maximal Arid Graphs
banked_reason: substrate-unbuildable: the frozen three-vertex maximal-arid nested/Gaussian classification remains the sole sorry after a real bounded attempt, and an independent validity gate found no bounded faithful route.

proof_attempt_summary: Two reusable substrate studies completed and promoted sorry-free finite-positive-table fixing and finite-DAG kernel-Markov APIs; the run then closed the binary source-membership and all-finite-alphabet separator components. A final managed proof attempt proved three graph-theoretic bow/aridity leaves, but the frozen headline still required the full at-most-three-vertex maximal-arid nested/Gaussian/Zariski classification. That paper-owned classification remained the sole sorry and could not be gated, studied away, or removed without weakening the source claim.
tldr: Gaussian algebraic inclusion is not a complete certificate for universal nested-Markov inclusion of maximal arid graphs. A four-variable source graph is contained in the target graph for every positive-definite Gaussian SEM covariance, yet a strictly positive rational binary source law violates a target fixing-derived Verma invariance by \(1/20\). A complete classification on at most three observed vertices proves that four vertices are minimal. The Gaussian test remains a necessary rejection filter, while the equality-only conjecture is unresolved.
gap: The literature proves universal nested inclusion implies Gaussian inclusion and conjectures the converse, but the reported experiment concerns algebraically equivalent pairs and does not test all ordered inclusion pairs. No complete cross-graph implication criterion for reachable fixing kernels was located.
fill: Give an independently auditable maximal-arid pair, an all-parameter residual map proving actual Gaussian SEM inclusion, an exact positive binary separator and finite-alphabet lift, and the resulting safe algorithmic interface; separately complete the at-most-three-variable classification if the smallest-case claim is to be made.
